meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/3H, Monday 10 June 2024, P76927A), downloaded from qualifications.pearson.com. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as EDEXCEL-JUN24-F-P3. The crossover block is 3F q22–q28 = 3H q1–q7, contiguous, and the marks match item for item (2, 4, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4). Note 3F q29 is NOT shared — the block stops at q28. All 21 (Total for Question) lines recovered and summing to the printed 80. Coded WITH mark_split.

coding_notes: q1–q7 are 3F q22–q28 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.
q12 tagged fractional_enlargements — the scale factor is negative, which is what that node covers alongside fractional ones. 3F q18a's half-turn rotation is a different item on a different node.
q13 tagged counting_without_listing: the mark scheme's routes are 30 × 29 ÷ 2 and the sum of the integers to 29, neither of which lists the pairs.
q17 tagged sequences, not growth_and_decay. The recurrence is given as h(n+1) = 0.55 h(n) and every mark is for iterating it; the item never asks for a rate or a multiplier to be identified.
q20b tagged simultaneous_equations_quadratic alongside sequences — the geometric condition produces a quadratic in y that the last two process marks form and simplify.

q21 tagged exact_trig_values then circumfrence_of_a_circle: both perimeters come from half-side lengths found with exact sine and tangent of 30 degrees, and the circle's circumference is what they are compared against.
q10 tagged algebraic_proof then ratio — the answer is a shown result in terms of x, and the ratio is the structure it is built on.
